newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WIN TOSS AND BAT V WEST INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PAKISTAN WIN TOSS AND BAT V WEST INDIES.

text.p: Pakistan captain Wasim Akram won the toss and elected to bat in the second match in the World Series limited overs final at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Monday.
Pakistan, who beat West Indies by four wickets in Sydney in the first of the best-of-three final series on Saturday, recalled opener Aamir Sohail.
Sohail was suspended from the first match for dissent and the left-hander replaced middle-order batsman Mujahid Jamshed.
Pakistan also called in fast bowler Shahid Nazir in favour of leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed.
West Indies fast bowler Curtly Ambrose passed a fitness test on his hamstring strain before the start and Carl Hooper was recalled to the middle order after his recovery from a shin injury.
Fast bowler Cameron Cuffy, who was summoned from the Caribbean to replace injured pacemen Kenneth Benjamin and Nixon McLean, started the match.

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Junior Murray, Brian Lara, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Phil Simmons, Roland Holder, Curtly Ambrose, Courtney Walsh (captain), Cameron Cuffy, Robert Samuels (12th man).

Pakistan - Aamir Sohail, Shahid Afridi, Zahoor Elahi, Ijaz Ahmed, Inzamam-ul-Haq, Mohammad Wasim, Moin Khan, Wasim Akram (captain), Saqlain Mushtaq, Waqar Younis, Shahid Nazir, Ijaz Ahmed Junior (12th man).
